summary: This is a Snowflake-style SQL reference page for the DESCRIBE PACKAGES POLICY command, which displays the details of a packages policy. It gives the syntax (DESC[RIBE] PACKAGES POLICY <name>), explains the name parameter and its quoting and case-sensitivity rules, and lists the access control requirements: OWNERSHIP on the packages policy, or USAGE to view it. The page ends with a single example, DESC PACKAGES POLICY packages_policy_prod_1;. Navigation and footer text were ignored.
one_line: Reference page for the SQL command DESCRIBE PACKAGES POLICY, which shows details of a packages policy and its required privileges.
key_facts: DESCRIBE can be abbreviated to DESC in the DESCRIBE PACKAGES POLICY command.
The syntax is DESC[RIBE] PACKAGES POLICY <name>.
The <name> parameter specifies the identifier for the packages policy to describe.
If a packages policy identifier contains spaces or special characters, the entire string must be enclosed in double quotes.
Identifiers enclosed in double quotes are case-sensitive.
The OWNERSHIP privilege on a packages policy is automatically granted to the role that created the object, but can be transferred.
The USAGE privilege on a packages policy enables viewing it in a SHOW or DESCRIBE command.
Operating on any object in a schema also requires the USAGE privilege on the parent database and schema.
The page's example command is DESC PACKAGES POLICY packages_policy_prod_1;.
The DESCRIBE PACKAGES POLICY command describes the details about a packages policy.
